summary.text: Molecular geometry is the three-dimensional arrangement of the atoms in a molecule, including its general shape, bond lengths, bond angles and torsional angles.
It influences properties of a substance such as its reactivity, polarity, phase of matter, color, magnetism and biological activity.
Geometries are best determined at low temperature, because at higher temperatures the molecular structure is averaged over more accessible geometries.

facts.label: Bond angle
facts.value: Angle formed between three atoms across at least two bonds

facts.label: Torsional angle
facts.value: Angle between the planes of the first and last three atoms

facts.label: Bond length
facts.value: Average distance between two bonded nuclei

items.prompt: Two compounds have the same chemical formula, but their atoms are connected in a different order. What would you expect?

options.label: Identical properties, since the formula is the same
Often different geometries and very different properties
That they are mirror images of each other
That only one of the two can be a stable substance

items.explain: Structural isomers have the same formula but atoms bonded in a different order, often forming alternate geometries with very different properties.

items.prompt: A chemist picks three atoms linked in a row and reports how widely the outer two open out around the middle one. Which quantity is that?

options.label: A torsional angle
A bond length
A dihedral plane
A bond angle

items.explain: A bond angle is the angle formed between three atoms across at least two bonds.

items.prompt: A chemist wants reliable molecular geometries from spectra and decides to cool the sample close to absolute zero. Why?

options.label: Warmer samples populate too many higher rotational states, blurring the average
Cold samples have longer bonds, which are easier to measure
Warmth makes molecules switch between solid and gas shapes
Cooling removes the electrons that confuse the measurement

items.explain: Spectra average over rotational states, and at higher temperatures too many higher rotational states are populated to extract reliable geometries.

items.prompt: A chemist wants to describe how the two ends of a four-atom chain are twisted relative to each other. Which measurement does this?

options.label: The average distance between the two end nuclei
The angle formed by three of the atoms across two bonds
The angle between the plane of the first three atoms and the last three
The total number of bonds in the chain

items.explain: For four atoms bonded in a chain, the torsional angle is the angle between the plane of the first three atoms and the plane of the last three.

items.prompt: Two molecules connect their atoms in the same order but are oriented differently in space, and their melting and boiling points are similar. What is true of them?

options.label: They are different molecules, which matters most for biochemical activity
They are the same molecule, since their melting points match
They are different only if their chemical formulas differ
They must differ widely in boiling point

items.explain: Stereoisomers may share many physicochemical properties but are still different molecules, especially when considering biochemical activity.

items.prompt: A chemist measures the shape of the same molecule as a solid, in solution and as a gas. What might she find?

options.label: The same shape in all three, since the atoms are fixed
A real shape only in the gas, with the others blurred
A geometry that can differ between the three states
A change only between solid and gas, never in solution

items.explain: The molecular geometry can be different as a solid, in solution and as a gas.
